dedupe_keys.name: data accompanying chapter 5 of the phd dissertation energy system design and operation of hydrogen fuelled ships

description: TU Delft provides Python simulation and analysis workflows for weather-driven variation in hydrogen-ship power demand, energy-system sizing and lifetime cost. Separate laden and ballast scripts combine vessel speed and course with daily ERA5 wind and wave inputs. Spreadsheet outputs support fuel-cell capacity histograms and cost distributions under hydrogen prices of 3, 6 and 9 US dollars per kilogram. The source identifies PySCIPOpt and the SCIP solver as dependencies. Coverage: No complete measurement interval or evaluation extent is stated in the reviewed source. Access: public native metadata describes the release and its formats. Licence: CC-BY-4.0. Cost and current distribution access remain unknown. Caveats: The bundle accompanies Chapter 5 of a dissertation and is distinct from the Chapter 3 retrofit model and Chapter 4 design optimisation. Thesis dates of 2022 to 2026 do not establish weather observation coverage. Source code, input arrays and cost assumptions were not reproduced.
inputs: Vessel speed and course, laden or ballast demand inputs, ERA5 wind and wave parameters.
name: Data accompanying Chapter 5 of the PhD Dissertation: Energy System Design and Operation of Hydrogen Fuelled Ships
notes: Metadata only. No linked files, executable source, dataset arrays, archives, images, instruction documents or external API data were acquired. Native source claims were not independently reproduced.
outputs: Weather-adjusted power profiles, capacity distributions and lifetime-cost distributions.
